Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a one-page MAP summary and a sizing sheet (see attachments). High-level answers below; happy to flesh out in the MAP checkpoint call.

POC (4–8 weeks) recommendation:
- GPU mix: 6x A100 80GB (NVLink) in us-west1; 2x A10G spare instances for low-cost throughput testing.
- Regions: Primary in us-west1 (latency to your EO site), lightweight mirror in us-east1 for failover.
- Throughput targets (POC): payload mix is 80% chat-like + 20% long-form; goal 8k tokens/sec sustained across pool, burst to 18k tokens/sec.

Production target (steady-state, Q3):
- GPU mix: 24x A100 80GB + optional 8x H100 80GB for higher concurrency endpoints and embedding-heavy workflows. We recommend reserving a 10% burst pool (dynamic routing to non-dedicated) to handle spikes.
- Regions: us-west1 primary, eu-west1 for EU traffic (if you need it we can provision a minimal region), us-east1 for DR.
- Throughput targets (production): 50k tokens/sec sustained across the dedicated pool, 140k tokens/sec burst capacity leveraging regional routing and autoscaling.

Notes:
- A100s give best price/perf for our quantized LLM variants and are easiest to manage for the private appliance we deploy; H100s are recommended only for heavy training-like workloads or if you need lower latency at very large batch sizes.
- We can switch mix toward H100s if Atlas requires sub-50ms tail latency at high concurrency — we'll run a short eval in the POC to confirm.

Action items I'm attaching: MAP_20270426_v1.pdf (timeline + checkpoints) and private_gpu_sizing_sheet.xlsx (per-region cost/throughput table).

Can we confirm a MAP checkpoint call for Tue 27 Apr 10:00 PT? If that works I’ll send calendar invite and a one-slide agenda.

Best,
Aditya Rao
